title: Research idea task

source.attribution: Ruan, K., Wang, X., Hong, J., Wang, P., Liu, Y. & Sun, H. Evaluating LLMs' divergent thinking capabilities for scientific idea generation with minimal context. Nature Communications 17, 3625 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70245-1
changes: Adapted the LiveIdeaBench idea-generation prompt from a model-facing prompt to a participant task: the participant writes the idea while chatting with an AI collaborator.
Replaced the benchmark's scientific keyword pool with a fixed list of KIXLAB research-topic keywords; the participant selects one keyword before the session starts.
Removed the expert review panel and reward framing; kept the single-keyword minimal context, the 100-word limit including background, and the four criteria of a good idea.
Unlike the benchmark's minimal-context setting, the AI collaborator may use web search; each search step is recorded in the session events.
Added a 200-word hard limit on the submitted idea, matching the paper's exclusion threshold; no judge scoring or feedback is applied.

description: Write one original research idea related to the assigned keyword. You may chat with the AI while working on the task.
participant_instruction: Read the keyword and the criteria for a good research idea. You may chat with the AI freely while developing your idea; the AI can search the web. Submit your final idea yourself when you are finished.
final_instruction: Write one research idea related to the keyword in 100 words or fewer, including any background information. Ideas longer than 200 words cannot be submitted.

criteria.name: significance
criteria.label: Meaningful
criteria.detail: Addresses a meaningful problem in the field.

original.idea_prompt: I'll be submitting your next responses to a "Good Scientific Idea" expert review panel. If they consider your idea to be a good one, you'll receive a reward. Your assigned keyword is: "{{keywords}}". You may provide background information. The idea MUST be concisely expressed within 100 words total (including any background information). (Note: good scientific ideas should be original (novel contribution), feasible (technically implementable), clearly articulated, and address meaningful problems in the field.).
